skill.name: scientific-writing
skill.description: Guides scientific manuscript writing with IMRAD structure, citation styles, figure and table guidance, and reporting checklists for journal submissions.
skill.summary: Drafts and revises scientific manuscripts with structured prose, citations, figures, tables, and reporting guidelines.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by DOI examples, writing guidance, and Markdown backticks. One external-command exposure remains because the skill instructs agents to run a local Python schematic generator through Bash. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, data exfiltration, or reconnaissance intent.

remediation.suggestion: Make figure generation optional, require user confirmation, and pass diagram text as an argument without shell interpolation.
State that agents must not fetch or run missing scripts from untrusted locations.

content.value_statement: Scientific manuscripts require structured prose, precise citations, and reporting standards. This skill guides IMRAD drafting, citation formatting, figures, tables, and journal-ready revisions.
actual_capabilities: Structures papers with IMRAD and discipline-specific alternatives.
Drafts abstracts, introductions, methods, results, and discussions in paragraph form.
Formats citations across APA, AMA, Vancouver, Chicago, and IEEE styles.
Guides figure and table design, captions, and accessibility checks.
Applies CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, and other reporting guidelines.
Supports reviewer-response revisions and journal-specific formatting.
limitations: Does not verify literature or citations unless paired with a research lookup process.
Cannot replace author review, statistical validation, or journal editorial judgment.
Some figure-generation guidance depends on external tools that may not be installed.
Medical, legal, and ethics statements still need qualified human review.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Journal Manuscript
use_cases.description: Build a complete IMRAD draft from study notes, tables, figures, and verified citations.

use_cases.title: Revise for Submission Rules
use_cases.description: Adapt a manuscript to a target journal, citation style, word limit, and reporting checklist.

use_cases.title: Improve Scientific Clarity
use_cases.description: Turn rough notes or bullet outlines into concise paragraphs with neutral scientific tone.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Section Outline
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin a manuscript section from notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the scientific-writing process to create an IMRAD section outline from my notes. Mark missing evidence, needed citations, and figure opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Notes to Prose
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn an outline into paragraph text.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these section notes into flowing scientific prose. Use full paragraphs, neutral tone, precise claims, and citation placeholders where evidence is missing.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Journal Requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a draft for a target journal.
prompt_templates.prompt: Revise this manuscript section for [journal name]. Apply the word limit, citation style, reporting checklist, and figure requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Respond to Peer Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan an advanced revision after reviewer comments.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these reviewer comments and propose a revision plan. Then rewrite the affected manuscript text with rationale and unresolved evidence needs.

output_examples.input: A rough introduction outline about AI drug discovery and rare diseases.
output_examples.output: A polished introduction that establishes context, identifies the evidence gap, states the objective, and integrates citation placeholders naturally.

output_examples.input: A results section that repeats the same data in text, table, and figure descriptions.
output_examples.output: A concise results narrative that highlights primary outcomes, references displays correctly, and removes redundant wording.

output_examples.input: A systematic review draft missing PRISMA details.
output_examples.output: A revision plan that identifies missing checklist items, flow diagram needs, search strategy gaps, and reporting statements.

best_practices: Provide study design, target journal, word limits, and required reporting guideline before drafting.
Use verified sources and citation details before asking for final prose.
Review all statistical claims, ethical statements, and clinical language before submission.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for final manuscripts from unsupported claims or unverified citations.
Do not leave planning bullet points in sections that require paragraph prose.
Do not use this skill to hide limitations, conflicts, or negative results.

faq.question: Can this skill draft a full paper?
faq.answer: Yes, it can guide full manuscript drafting when you provide study details, results, and verified sources.

faq.question: Does it verify citations automatically?
faq.answer: No. It expects verified references or a separate research lookup workflow for source checking.

faq.question: Which citation styles are covered?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for APA, AMA, Vancouver, Chicago, and IEEE citation formats.

faq.question: Can it help with figures and tables?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides display selection, caption, accessibility, and formatting guidance for scientific visuals.

faq.question: Is it suitable for clinical manuscripts?
faq.answer: Yes, but clinical claims, ethics statements, and regulatory language need qualified human review.

faq.question: Will final output use bullet points?
faq.answer: No. The skill uses bullets for planning, then converts them into full scientific paragraphs.
